claims.claim: A June 30, 2026 arXiv paper finds that contracts settling on a movable asset price transfer wealth to manipulators and harm underlying price discovery, and that Polymarket's five-minute Bitcoin contract showed settlement-time order-flow spikes, reversals, and retail-funded manipulator profits largely absent in fifteen-minute contracts.
claims.episode_span: After Polymarket launched a five-minute Bitcoin contract, settlement-time spot order flow spiked.
claims.supporting_quote: After the launch of Polymarket's five-minute Bitcoin contract, settlement-time spot order flow spikes, causing large price reversals after settlement. Manipulators capture a large amount of profit, mostly from retail. Manipulation is largely absent in the fifteen-minute contracts: lengthening the contract horizon removes it, providing the market-design remedy our model and evidence support.

claims.claim: A January 28, 2026 arXiv paper using agent-based simulation finds that whale traders can temporarily shift prediction-market prices in proportion to their capital share, with larger and longer distortions when other bettors herd and learn slowly.
claims.episode_span: Theory in the paper says whales shift prices in proportion to their share of market capital.
claims.source_title: Manipulation in Prediction Markets: An Agent-based Modeling Experiment
claims.supporting_quote: Our theoretical analysis corroborates these results, showing that whales can shift prices proportionally to their share of market capital, with distortion duration depending on non-whale learning rates and herding intensity.
